title: runtime-validate-response-schemas-and-stream-rewind
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds a runtime-level JSON Schema validator for response_format-based structured output and a streaming rewind+retry path for OpenAI-compat streaming. Motivation: users running in strict schema mode need deterministic validation errors while still benefiting from streaming; previously a schema failure in the middle of a stream simply produced a truncated or invalid payload and an opaque error. This PR implements a low-overhead validator that runs on streamed chunks, detects schema divergence as early as possible, provides a compact machine-readable validation_failures payload, and when configured to 'rewind_on_schema_failure' will rewind the stream to the last safe token boundary, request an on-the-fly correction from the model (via a short re-prompt), and replay a corrected substream to the client. Changes include: runtime validator, OpenAI-compat transport hooks, SDK helpers for Python/TS, docs + examples, and end-to-end tests. Checklist: - [x] implement streaming validator with incremental checks - [x] add rewind+retry mechanism with backoff & max_retries config - [x] expose response_format validation errors to API clients (structured) - [x] add SDK ergonomics (helpers to set strict_mode, rewind_on_schema_failure) - [x] update standard OpenAI-compat behavior to return structured validation metadata when compatibility mode is enabled - [x] add unit/integration tests and docs examples - [x] safety review for prompt-repair flow Links: Linear: ENG-3120, Docs PR: #1327 (external), Design note: https://linear.app/redwood/notes/ENG-3120/streaming-schema-rewind (internal). This description is intentionally continuous and compact.

review_conversation: Marco Li (review): Can you clarify the performance impact on 8k context models? Suggest a microbenchmark and a config knob to disable streaming validation on high-throughput routes.

Aisha Patel (author): Added a microbenchmark in tests/benchmarks and added 'validation_enabled' per-route config. See serving/runtime/schema_validator.go for fast-path checks that avoid allocations when disabled.
Rima Das (review): We're exposing a structured 'validation_failures' field to clients. Need to ensure it doesn't leak internal tokens in PII-sensitive flows.

Aisha Patel (author): Validation metadata is redacted by default and can emit a high-level enum + field path. Full error details are gated behind enterprise telemetry and only returned when 'expose_validation_details' is enabled (opt-in for Private/Dedicated customers).
Evan Thompson (review): Tests look good. Please add a migration note for existing OpenAI-compat users; the compatibility transport changes headers.
Aisha Patel (author): Added docs/guides/structured-output.md migration section and the SDK helpers to automatically adapt existing calls.
release_notes: Add runtime streaming JSON Schema validation with optional rewind+retry behavior. New API knobs: response_format.strict (boolean), response_format.rewind_on_schema_failure (boolean). Structured validation failures are returned in OpenAI-compat responses under 'validation_failures' when enabled. See docs/guides/structured-output.md for migration steps.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: additional CPU on streaming paths for prefix validation. Mitigation: validation is opt-in per-route, fast-path guard to skip allocation when disabled, and a config to only validate on sampled requests. Rewind path limited to small correction window and capped retries to avoid increased tail latency.
docs_impact: Added detailed guide: docs/guides/structured-output.md, updated OpenAI-compat migration notes and SDK example snippets in python and typescript.
testing_summary: New unit tests for incremental validator, integration tests that repro schema divergence mid-stream, and e2e scenario that exercises rewind+repair against a mocked LLM. Benchmarks show ~3-7% cpu increase when validation is enabled on 4xA10 routes; disabled-by-default for high-throughput tiers.
security_review: prompt-repair flow reviewed by security. Repair prompts are templated and sanitized; no raw client prompt content is appended to repair requests. Audit log entries added for any automatic repair actions.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated: enable on Hosted API for a limited set of customers for the initial rollout. Notify SRE on rollout to Dedicated clusters to watch tail latency. Docs and SDK releases must land alongside this merge.
examples: examples/structured-output/rewind_example.py: demonstrates strict mode with rewind_on_schema_failure and how to parse validation_failures
examples/structured-output/rewind_example.ts: TS SDK example that toggles strict mode and shows client-side fallback
